themes.reason: States the core objective (sustainable exploitation at MSY, stock health) and directly explains why the national ban was chosen as the means to achieve it; without this the rationale for the intervention disappears.

Lays out the do-nothing, IFCA byelaw, seasonal ban and national ban alternatives and explains why each was rejected in favour of the national SI ban; this comparative justification is the backbone of the proposal argument.

Shows that the existing voluntary v-notching scheme has been tried and has failed to achieve sufficient uptake, which is the key evidence justifying why a mandatory ban (rather than continued voluntary action) is needed.

Provides detailed quantification of costs to fishers and government, supporting the should-explain point on costs/benefits, but the rationale for choosing the ban does not depend on these specific figures standing.
Supplies the modelling evidence that the ban will lead to stock recovery and higher landings, which is the key evidence base underpinning the claim that this intervention will solve overfishing.
Details assumptions about existing IFCA bans and compliance used in the cost modelling; background detail that supports but is not essential to the core choice rationale.
Notes data gaps (e.g. North-West functional unit) affecting cost estimates; a minor caveat rather than a pillar of the proposal argument.

Explains why the government proceeded with national legislation rather than waiting for EU-wide measures; relevant context but a secondary justification rather than the central reason for the chosen intervention.
Presents aggregated net cost/benefit figures that summarise the cost analysis; derivative of other themes rather than an independent support for the choice of intervention.
Restates the long-term landing benefits already covered in the stock recovery modelling theme; duplicative rather than a distinct pillar of the argument.
Reiterates enforcement advantages of the national ban over IFCA byelaws already covered under Policy Options Considered; useful detail but not a separate core support.
Summarises the preferred option and headline figures already established elsewhere; it restates rather than adds independent support for the proposal.
